name: Hydra
introduction: is the Water Snake, the largest of the 88 constellations. It stretches across more than 100 degrees of sky, from its head near Cancer to its tail beside Libra. In myth, it is either the serpent killed by Hercules or the water snake blamed by Apollo’s crow. It is best seen on northern spring evenings.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: Hydra is long but dim, with only one bright star. [Alphard](hip:46390), “the solitary one”, is an orange giant 180 light-years away that shines alone in a region with no other bright stars.

One of the Sun’s nearest neighbors also lies in Hydra: [WISE 0855−0714](id:wise-0855-0714), a brown dwarf about 7 light-years away, discovered in 2014. It is the coldest object known outside the Solar System that formed like a star, about as cold as the North Pole in winter, with clouds that may contain water ice.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: The snake’s head is a small group of stars including [Ashlesha](hip:43109), [Zeta Hydrae](hip:43813) and [Delta Hydrae](hip:42313). [Theta Hydrae](hip:45336) has a white dwarf companion.
[Gamma Hydrae](hip:64962), near the tail, and [Zhang](hip:48356), in the middle of the body, are yellow giants.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: The large planetary nebula [Abell 35](id:abell-35) surrounds a star near the snake’s tail. Hydra also contains the Southern Pinwheel Galaxy, M83, the Ghost of Jupiter, NGC 3242, the clusters M48 and M68, and, far beyond, the Hydra Cluster of galaxies.
